raw_segments.text: The commercial ties which unite the Confederate states are strengthened by the increasing
manufacturers of the Americans, and the union which began to exist in their opinions gradually
forms a part of their habits.
The course of time has swept away the bugbear thoughts which haunted the imaginations of
The federal power is not become oppressive.
It has not destroyed the independence of the states.
It has not subjected the Confederates to monarchial institutions, and the union has not rendered
the lesser states dependent upon the larger ones, but the confederation has continued
to increase in population, in wealth, and in power.
I am therefore convinced that the natural obstacles to the continuance of the American
Union are not so powerful at the present time as they were in 1789, and that the enemies
of the union are not so numerous.
